assessment.summary: BRAF (P15056) is one of the most extensively validated oncology drug targets in human medicine, with 5 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 11,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 138 PDB structures including many high-resolution ligand-bound complexes. The target is highly druggable with a well-characterised ATP-binding pocket and a wealth of structural, chemical, and clinical evidence supporting continued drug discovery efforts.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 66.4 (55% high-confidence fraction) suggests disordered regions outside the kinase domain, but this does not impair druggability given the extensive experimental structural data

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., BRAF V600E paradoxical activation, splice variants, RAS-independent dimerisation) are well-known but next-generation inhibitor strategies targeting these remain an active and partially unresolved area
Structural coverage of BRAF in non-V600E mutant contexts (e.g., class II/III mutations, fusions) may be less complete than for the canonical V600E form
Allosteric and dimer-interface inhibitor binding modes are less structurally characterised compared to ATP-competitive binding
Long-term clinical resistance profiles and combination strategies are still being defined in several tumour types (e.g., colorectal, biliary tract)
